free_tier.stated: No published byte quota. The platform documents hosting over 5 petabytes of data across 330+ products from 130+ organizations, serving approximately 700 TB per month for public data publishing. Documentation specifies no per-product, per-account, or per-file cap.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: No retention clause documented in available terms.

egress.terms: Free and unmetered in practice for the reader: anonymous GET with no credentials, Cloudflare in front, R2/Turbo-adjacent CDN headers. No egress meter appears anywhere in the docs.

tooling: Genuine S3 proxy. Endpoint https://data.source.coop, --no-sign-request for reads. Upload credentials are Source-issued but in AWS format and valid only at the proxy; path is s3://<account-id>/<product-id>/ and you cannot write outside your own prefix. Accepts aws cli, boto3, rclone with a custom endpoint, plus a Source CLI and service accounts for CI.
chaining: Multiplier is data products per account/org, and orgs can hold team members. Because reads are anonymous and S3-native, this is the cleanest 'someone else's S3 on a real CDN' shape in the whole D area. It can be mounted by AList/rclone and fronted by Cloudflare exactly per §2.1.
limits_note: Write-gated. Publishing data requires application to the beta testing program via web form. Future flat pricing is announced for upcoming release. Data repositories are public by default with no private mode.
reliability_note: Beta + announced-but-unpublished pricing means the free window has an unknown end date. Store only data that has a second home.
confidence_note: Unverified: carried from historical research records without live verification. A first-party page read confirms documentation.

evidence.proved: PROBED (this is the new evidence): curl -qsS -D - -> HTTP 200, Content-Length: 16187, Accept-Ranges: bytes, ETag, Last-Modified, Server: cloudflare, CF-Cache-Status: DYNAMIC. Downloaded twice and SHA-256 compared: cdd18d37e1af2320c2eaa763a6b70a8258a1ee2e5dc78e558ea0922e981e56d6 on both copies, and 16,187 bytes on disk matches the declared Content-Length — a true roundtrip, not a 200-with-empty-body.
PROBED: curl -H 'Range: bytes=0-99' on the same object -> HTTP 206 Partial Content, Content-Range: bytes 0-99/16187, 100 bytes body. Range requests work, so resumable/parallel fetches are viable.

extras.agent_focus: 2026-era research-data and data-marketplace platforms, deliberately judged on the BINDING constraint (does a person with only an email get past the write gate?) rather than on the marketing quota. Coverage: IEEE DataPort (the wave-7 discovery this slot confirms and extends), Mozilla Data Collective (2025 launch, the only new ≥100 GB-per-file free host found), Source Cooperative re-probed at the byte level, the French national Dataverse (Recherche Data Gouv) as the one genuinely EU-funded space with a self-serve email account, plus the 2026 data-marketplace entrants (Snowflake, Databricks Free Edition, data.world, Datarade, Tableland, Spice.ai, DataChain), the EU Data Spaces (Gaia-X / Catena-X / EOSC EU Node / DICE) and ResearchGate/Academia.edu data upload. Two structural results dominate: (a) the 'data marketplace' category is uniformly not storage — they are catalogues, and every one of them fails on per-object size by two to three orders of magnitude; (b) the EU Data Spaces are real and large but gated on eduGAIN/eIDAS identity, so they are closed on identity exactly like CSC Allas and LUMI-O before them.
